justification: GATE-2: _detect_sepp_lep_overrides created a height/FSR SEPP override on a bare numeric '>' comparison, ignoring std.eligible and heritage. The Low/Mid-Rise Housing reforms exclude heritage items and Heritage Conservation Areas, yet the engine applied a 7m->9.5m / 3-storey bonus on the Haberfield HCA — an over-report of impermissible height/density on protected land. The override is now created only for eligible standards and never on heritage land (the LEP control stands).

pre_impl.existing_data: SEPPStandard already carries an 'eligible' bool (constraint_models.py:46) but _detect_sepp_lep_overrides never read it; heritage presence is available at both override call sites via controls['heritage_items'] (Portal) and heritage_postgis['has_heritage'] (PostGIS), but was never passed to the override logic.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: 'eligible' is computed from LOT SIZE ONLY (_build_sepp_housing:1643), so it does not capture the heritage exclusion. Honouring eligible alone would NOT fix Haberfield (793 m2 > min -> eligible=True); an explicit heritage gate is required.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new data source: _detect_sepp_lep_overrides gains an is_heritage flag and an eligibility check; a pure _is_heritage_land(controls, heritage_postgis) helper derives the flag from data already fetched. Both assembly paths pass it.
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A - both helpers are pure and consume data already fetched upstream; a Portal/PostGIS failure upstream is unchanged and, if heritage data is missing, is_heritage is False (the override may apply) — heritage data quality is a separate gate, not regressed here.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A - backend override detection only; the SeppLepOverride list type is unchanged, so no frontend boundary shifts. The capacity card stays unexposed.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: If heritage data is absent for a genuinely-heritage parcel, the override could still apply (over-report) — but that is a heritage-data-coverage gap, not introduced here; where heritage data exists the override is correctly suppressed. The conservative direction (suppress on any detected heritage) never over-reports on known-heritage land.

functions.name: _detect_sepp_lep_overrides
functions.input: the SEPP standards list, the LEP height and FSR values, and an is_heritage flag
functions.output: override records only for eligible standards strictly more generous than the LEP, and none at all on heritage land
functions.if_none: on heritage land it returns an empty list immediately; otherwise ineligible standards are skipped

functions.name: _is_heritage_land
functions.input: the parsed planning controls dict and the optional PostGIS heritage result
functions.output: True when the parcel is a heritage item or sits in a Heritage Conservation Area, else False
functions.if_none: missing or empty heritage data returns False (no detected heritage)

values: N/A - no regulatory values hardcoded; the override compares SEPP standard values already fetched from the DB against the LEP values from the Portal, and reads the existing eligible flag.
queries: N/A - no database queries added; both helpers operate on data already fetched by the brief (sepp_housing, controls, heritage_postgis).

break_it.scenario: A SEPP height bonus fires on a Heritage Conservation Area parcel (the Haberfield case)
break_it.what_happens: Pre-GATE-2 a 7m->9.5m / 3-storey override inflated the whole capacity on protected land where the reform does not apply
break_it.how: the function returns [] immediately when is_heritage; test_heritage_suppresses_override asserts no override

break_it.scenario: An ineligible SEPP standard (e.g. lot too small) still tries to override the LEP
break_it.what_happens: An override would apply from a standard the parcel does not qualify for
break_it.how: the loop skips standards where not std.eligible; test_ineligible_standard_does_not_override asserts []

break_it.scenario: A genuinely eligible non-heritage parcel must still receive the SEPP bonus
break_it.what_happens: Over-suppressing the override would under-report a valid Low/Mid-Rise height uplift on eligible non-heritage land
break_it.how: the override is created when eligible, not heritage, and strictly more generous; test_eligible_height_bonus_overrides_lep_when_not_heritage asserts one height override

break_it.scenario: Heritage is recorded only in PostGIS, not the Portal heritage_items
break_it.what_happens: A Portal-only check would miss HCA coverage that comes from the PostGIS heritage layer
break_it.how: _is_heritage_land checks BOTH controls['heritage_items'] and heritage_postgis['has_heritage']; both-source tests assert True

break_it.scenario: SEPP value equals the LEP value (not strictly greater)
break_it.what_happens: A non-uplift could be mis-recorded as an override
break_it.how: the strict '>' comparison is preserved; test_no_override_when_sepp_not_strictly_greater asserts []

post_merge.manual_verify: Re-run the Haberfield brief and confirm NO 7m->9.5m SEPP height override and no 3-storey inflation (the LEP 7m stands). GATE-1 part 2 (zone-derived dev_type) and GATE-3 (site-coverage cap, no silent drop) remain. Engine stays unexposed (#513 unmerged) until the legality gates complete.
